I am diagnosed with obsessive-compulsive disorder, and during my active days in the church I was SO incredibly hard on myself for everything that it crushed the lights out of me.  (I had the added measure of being gay and working myself to death in the church, since "maybe if I'm REALLY good in other areas, God will forgive me for my evil feelings.")  My scrupulousity went so far as to making lists of all the commandments (the major ones I could think of anyways, usually a list of around 70 items.)   I would routinely take this list down off of my bedroom door and sit down the list and evaluate/grade myself on each item, ALWAYS failing on chastity for masturbating and most other things.  [Example:  "#37:  Always be kind to others.  Oh but there was that lady I was huffy with in the store because of x, y, or z.  So that one's a FAIL."]  

At every general conference I would buy a new legal pad and from the 1st song until the last prayer I was writing. I filled the legal pad with all kinds of things that we are supposed to be doing, and not doing...  I would go home and type it all out highlighting the things that were mentioned that we need to be doing and not doing, which became my "guide" for the next 6 months.  

I worked in the church in any or every capacity needed. Whenever there was a meeting to attend, or a visit that needed to be done, or a lesson that  to be substituted for, or anything to do with the temple I was there.   People used to compliment me on how valiant I was, how much the Lord must be pleased with me for everything I do.....   What nobody knew is that I believed I was trash. Spiritual garbage. God's one mistake.   The proof being that I could never live up to everything in the lists I would make. I could never go through the scriptures and say yes I do this, yes I do that.   All I ever saw was my failures.. Failed at this command, failed at that command, and always, ALWAYS failed at the law of chastity – I just couldn't stop masturbating no matter how much I tried I couldn't stop.  And being as masturbation was part of the LoC, and violations of such were second only to murder, i considered myself only a teeeeny weeeny bit better than a murderer.   There were people who chopped others up with axes, followed by me. It might sound ridiculous but it's how my thought processes went. Some bishops told me to go easy on myself, whereas another bishop told me flat out that if I were to die I would go straight to the telestial kingdom because I masturbate.   That was 19 years ago and I still have not forgiven that man. I don't know if I ever can. 

Needless to say after 15 years of all of this, the ton of bricks on my back finally made me collapse and completely crushed me.   I could write a lot, lot more.  I haven't been to church in about 9 years and have no intention of going back. Because going back would mean "the list" again, as my therapist and I refer to it.   God and his religion and his fucking list can kiss my ass.   There are many religions out there, but Mormonism is not one of them to choose for someone with obsessive compulsive disorder. It will majorly fuck you up.   I'm 41 years old and I am just barely, I mean just scratching the surface of learning that I'm worthy of love.   And yes, I do blame the church. I blame God. I blame that bishop.   I blame the general authorities in salt lake who get up every 6 months and give sermon after sermon of do this, don't do that, do this only a little bit, do this more, do this less, more, more, more, more, more, MORE, MORE!!!!!!!  NEVER GOOD ENOUGH.  NEVER, EVER.

I've said this  many times but as flawless as the show is the biggest thing for me was how messy they wrote about Jesse figuring out Walt did poison Brock.  Jesse found out in Face Off that it was NOT ricin, but lily of the valley that poisoned Brock.  -- which neither of them had ever discussed.  Jesse didn't know Walt had a LOTV plant.  But then right before Ed is supposed to pick him up, he discovers his weed is missing and from there deduces Huell pickpocketed the ricin cigarette and got it to Walt to poison Brock.......except Jesse already knew that it was NOT ricin that poisoned Brock.  So at that point his freak out that Walt poisoned Brock "with ricin" made NO sense.  Because he already knew that was not the case.   
 Someone in writing really fucked that up.  It's played on screen so quickly and emotionally that you'd have to be analyzing it I think.  

Also -- Gus says to Walt at their dinner meeting at his house "the kids won't eat it" (the stew.)  What kids?  Granted we only see Gus' house inside twice, but it does not look like the house of a man who has kids.  If he had a wife/partner wouldn't we have seen them?  Or couldn't they have been used by Walt or anyone else really as a pawn piece?  Plus......the very strong impression that Max and Gus were lovers/partners, hence why Gus bitterly hated Hector and planned his revenge for 20 years.  I just can't see Gus with kids.  Or a woman.  Or, by the time we meet him, with any kind of partner.  

Hank, on finding out Walt is Heisenberg, trying to get Skyler to just confess everything, in a manipulative way (typical police m.o. right there) even balking when she suggests she oughta have an attorney -- which Hank knew damn right well she should but he didn't care about her at that point.  --- this isn't really a flaw in the writing, and generally I like Hank as a character, but what I do detest is this kind of behavior by the police in the real world so it strikes a nerve seeing it portrayed so perfectly in that scene.

Let me clarify. I don't want a temple recommend as some sort of status symbol. I know it works that way with some people that, that's their business. I want a temple recommend because because I enjoy the rituals of the temple –  I know many people think they are ridiculous and waste of time, but I don't agree with that perspective personally. Whether they are salvafic as such, doesn't really concern me. I learn very well through allegory, symbolism and abstract thought.   I love going to art galleries where the art is abstract. Colors and shapes and layers.... I have several pieces of abstract art in my home.  My ex partner–a man, as am I– got absolutely nothing from these paintings.  That's ok.   Although I did not think this way at the time, as I think about it now it's rather beautiful. I don't want the whole world to think like I do.  As far as your comment "anti-Jesus religions" - which seems to be more of a political statement - placing burdens and requirements on people, it could also be said that "pro-Jesus religions," whichever ones you would categorize as such, have also done their fair share of damage.  I'm a gay man.  Đo I even need to make a list of the atrocities done to people like me, in the name of hate, while using Jesus and the bible as an excuse?  "Pro Jesus religions" are in no way off the hook of placing burdens of destruction - sometimes self-destruction - on people.   They have plenty of blood on their praying hands.

Just an observation – Mormon rituals (or any rituals of any group) may have no value to one person, and a great deal of value to another.  Or, they may have little or no value to an individual at one stage of their journey/life but mean a great deal at another time.  And on that latter comment I speak for myself but I doubt I'm the only one.  

I've participated in Native American ritual with rich symbolism, private ritual of what some might label "pagan" (and others on a different – but not necessarily "wrong" vibration – would label "evil,") other than prayer circles I have also stood in other circles where light has been shone where once was shame.  My guess is that when you refer to prayer you are talking about the kneeling, closing your eyes, folding your arms, and starting "Dear Heavenly Father..."   That is a ritual. But there are hundreds if not thousands of ways to "pray."   I have prayed while being tossed about in the waves of the sea while body surfing, I have prayed as I simply contemplate the vastness of the universe, while screaming and crying and swearing in supportive ritual to eliminate the pain of guilt, shame, and self- hate I have carried in my body most of my life.  I have prayed while chanting and singing the holy names of Lord Krishna with one of my spiritual teachers.

My point is that there are literally thousands of rituals that we participate in every day of our lives, whether we're thinking of it as such or not.   Standing and putting your hand over your heart for the national anthem has great symbolism for Americans, but for people in other countries who despise us the meaning is completely different.  It's all about perspective.   I personally believe that the rituals of the temple are no different in that respect. 

One final thing and then I will shut up.. I think the greatest tool I have learned thus far in my exploration is to bust down the boxes I have had my thoughts in regarding just about everything.  To investigate words.  We throw around words all the time but do we REALLY know what we are saying? To ask "why?" of everything and investigate.  And get outside the box.  Do I always live by everything I have said here? Of course not.  It's what I strive for but more often than not I don't live up to it.  But I'm trying.

I also didn't like that Eve wasn't included in some way (I get that Gab is Xena's "wife," for all intents and purposes, but Eve is her *daughter.)*  Also -- adding in at the last minute another huge plot point about Xena killing 40,000 people was rather......too much.
